_about: Movement routines: tested building blocks for experiences. A step with "routine": "<name>" takes the routine's title, lines, figure, cues (or breath pattern), timing and closing line, unless the step sets its own. Personalize with "cueText": {"<index>": "new words"} to change what a cue says while keeping its pose and timing. Every routine is checked frame by frame with `node tools/routines.mjs`. Keys starting with _ are notes, not routines.

cat-stretch.title: Wake up like a cat
cat-stretch.purpose: Morning stiffness, low energy, waking the body with pleasure.
cat-stretch.needs: room to stand and reach overhead
cat-stretch.cautions: Tighten gently, never to strain. Skip the backward arch with a sore lower back.
lines: A cat never stretches to be productive. It stretches because it feels good.
Tighten a little first, then lengthen slowly, then let go completely. Sitting at the edge of a chair works too.
cat-stretch.ready: Stand up, or sit at the edge of your seat. Begin when you're ready.

cues.text: If a yawn wants to come, let it. Yawning is the body's own stretch.
Make two loose fists and draw your arms in close. Gently tighten everything, as if you were curling up.
Now slowly unfold. Arms long overhead, fingers wide, your spine reaching up.
Stretch like the biggest yawn of the year, all the way out to the edges. Let a sound out if one comes.
And let it all go. Arms drop. Feel the difference.
Right arm up and over to the left. Open the whole right side, from your fingertips down to your hip.
Slowly back to center.
Left arm up and over to the right. Long through the whole left side.
Back to center. Let everything hang loose.
Bend your knees a little and rest your hands on your thighs. Round your back like a cat, chin toward your chest.
Now the other way: let your belly drop, chest forward, and look ahead.
Once more, round and arch, as slowly as feels good.
Find one place that still feels tight, and give it a stretch of its own. Your way, no rules.

cat-stretch.after: Notice how your body feels now, compared with a few minutes ago.

side-stretch.title: Open both sides
side-stretch.purpose: Tight ribs, shallow breath, sitting too long.
side-stretch.cautions: Lean only as far as stays comfortable in the lower back.
lines: Standing or sitting tall. Follow the figure, or move however feels good.

cues.text: Feet under your hips, knees soft, arms loose.
Sweep both arms out to the sides and all the way up.
Bring your right arm up and over toward the left. Let your left hand slide down your leg. Breathe into your right ribs.
Back to the middle.
Left arm up and over toward the right. Right hand slides down. Breathe into your left ribs.
Let both arms float down.

side-stretch.after: Notice how much room there is in your breath now.

cat-cow-standing.title: Cat and cow, standing
cat-cow-standing.purpose: A stiff back and a busy mind: rhythmic movement that loosens the spine and paces the breath.
cat-cow-standing.needs: room to bend forward a little
cat-cow-standing.cautions: Keep the arch small with a sensitive lower back. Seated version: hands on your knees at the edge of a chair.
lines: Knees soft, hands resting on your thighs. Let the breath set the pace.

cues.text: Bend your knees a little and rest your hands on your thighs, back long and flat.
Breathing out, round your back up toward the ceiling and tuck your chin.
Breathing in, let your belly drop, lift your chest and look ahead.
Keep going at the pace of your breath. Round as you breathe out, arch as you breathe in.
Come back to a flat back, then roll up slowly to standing.

cat-cow-standing.after: Stand still for a moment and feel your spine.

roll-down.title: Roll down, roll up
roll-down.purpose: Releasing the back and neck; a reset after sitting; slowing down.
roll-down.cautions: Knees soft the whole time. Skip or go only halfway with high blood pressure, glaucoma or dizziness.
lines: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft. Go only as far down as feels good.

cues.text: Let your chin drop toward your chest.
Let the weight of your head draw you down, one bone at a time. Shoulders, then upper back.
Keep rolling down. Knees bend as much as they need to. Let your arms and head hang.
Hang here. Maybe sway a little, or nod your head yes and no.
Slowly roll back up, stacking one bone on top of the other. Your head comes up last.
Stand tall and let your breath settle.

roll-down.after: Notice the length in your back.

neck-release.title: Let the neck go
neck-release.purpose: Screen tension, a heavy head, holding stress in the shoulders and jaw.
neck-release.cautions: Small and slow. No full circles, and stop at any tingling or dizziness.
lines: Sitting or standing tall. Move slowly, and only as far as is easy.

cues.text: Let your shoulders drop away from your ears. Unclench your jaw.
Tip your right ear toward your right shoulder. Let the weight of your head do the work.
Back to center.
Left ear toward your left shoulder. Breathe into the right side of your neck.
Back to center.
Let your chin sink toward your chest. Feel the back of your neck lengthen.
Bring your head back up, slowly, until it feels balanced on top of your spine.

neck-release.after: Notice how your head sits on your shoulders now.

arm-circles.title: Big arm circles
arm-circles.purpose: Warming the shoulders, raising energy, loosening the upper back.
arm-circles.cautions: Keep the circles comfortable, smaller if a shoulder complains.
lines: Standing, feet planted. Slow and smooth, like drawing big circles in the air.

cues.text: Bring both arms forward, then up, then out wide, then down. One big, slow circle.
Keep circling. Let your breath follow: in as the arms rise, out as they come down.
Now reverse: out wide, up, forward and down.
Let your arms hang and feel the warmth in your shoulders.

shake-out.title: Shake it out
shake-out.purpose: Restless or tired-and-wired energy, after stress or conflict; discharge before settling.
shake-out.needs: room to move; seated works too
shake-out.cautions: Keep it loose and small at first. Seated: shake your hands and bounce your knees.
lines: Knees soft, everything loose. There's no wrong way to do this.

cues.text: Start by shaking out your hands, like flicking off water.
Let it spread to your arms and shoulders.
Now a gentle bounce through your knees, so the whole body jiggles.
Let your jaw go loose. Add a sound if one wants out.
And stop. Stand still and feel the buzz.

march.title: March in place
march.purpose: Flat, sluggish or numb; bringing energy up gently and rhythmically.
march.cautions: Lift your knees only as high as is comfortable; hold a chair or wall for balance if needed.
lines: Stand where you can move a little. Keep a hand on a chair if you'd like the balance.

cues.text: Start marching on the spot, lifting one knee, then the other, arms swinging.
Lift your knees a little higher, if that feels good.
Let the rhythm wake you up. Breathe out on every other step.
Slow down, step by step.
And come to stillness.

march.after: Feel your heart and your breath. That's your energy, awake.

sit-to-stand.title: Sit, stand, repeat
sit-to-stand.purpose: Low energy, a heavy body, wanting to feel strong; gentle strength that wakes the legs.
sit-to-stand.cautions: Go as low as is comfortable; sitting fully down each time is fine. Stop with knee pain.
lines: Stand in front of a chair, feet a little wider than your hips.

cues.text: Reach your arms forward and sit your hips back, as if to sit down. Lightly touch the chair.
Press through your feet and stand all the way up.
Again: down slowly, up with energy. Breathe out as you rise.
Stand tall. Feel your legs, strong and warm.

breath-of-joy.title: Breath of Joy
breath-of-joy.purpose: Flat, low energy, morning; a fast, playful lift.
breath-of-joy.cautions: Slow down or breathe normally if light-headed. Keep the fold small with high blood pressure, glaucoma or after a head injury.
lines: Three quick sips of air with your arms: forward, out wide, and up. Then a big "ha!" as you swing them down and soften your knees.
If you feel light-headed, slow down or breathe normally.
breath-of-joy.ready: feet a little wider than your hips

one-song-dance.title: One song
one-song-dance.purpose: Enliven, savor, play; a natural peak.
one-song-dance.needs: a song they love (or one they can sing or hum), a little space
one-song-dance.cautions: Any size of movement counts, including seated.
lines: Put on one song you love, the kind that makes your body want to move. Or sing one you know.
The music leads. Glance here if you want a nudge, and come back when the song ends.
one-song-dance.ready: The room is yours. Press play, then Begin.

cues.text: Start small. Let one part of you answer the music: a finger, your head, a foot.
Let it travel. Shoulders. Ribs. Hips.
No one is watching. There's nothing to get right.
Let it get bigger. Arms. Feet. Take up space.
Sing along, hum, laugh. Make whatever sound wants out.
Are you enjoying this? You don't have to be. Just notice.
Let the rest of the song carry you all the way to the end.

one-song-dance.after: Let the song end. Stand still and feel what's still moving.

self-holding.title: Holding yourself
self-holding.purpose: Activated, tender, self-critical; soothing through touch and warmth.
self-holding.needs: nothing; sitting or lying down is fine
self-holding.cautions: If touch doesn't feel safe today, rest your hands on your lap instead.

lineage.name: Self-holding and soothing touch
lineage.source: Peter Levine; Kristin Neff and Christopher Germer

lines: Sitting or standing, however you're most comfortable.

cues.text: Place one hand on your heart, and the other on your belly.
Feel the warmth of your hands. Let them be heavy.
Notice your breath moving under your hands, without changing it.
Stay as long as feels right. Something in you might soften, or not. Either is fine.
When you're ready, let your hands come to rest.

seated-arrival.title: Arriving in your seat
seated-arrival.purpose: Before a sit, inquiry or writing; finding a stable, upright, easy posture.
seated-arrival.cautions: Any comfortable position works, including lying down.
lines: On a chair or a cushion, however you can be upright and at ease.

cues.text: Feel what's underneath you: the seat, the floor, the ground holding you up.
Let your spine rise gently, as if a thread lifted the crown of your head.
Let your shoulders and hands rest. Soften your face.
Let your breath find its own rhythm. Nothing to do.
